title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-14
notes:
West leads the ♦A against 6♠. West wins the first trick and continues diamonds. South breathes a sigh of relief when East follows. A spade finesse wins.

If spades are 3-2 there will be no problem. South should gear his play towards handling 4-1 spades. There are two alternative lines to consider.

In the first alternative, South continues with the ♣K and overtakes with the ♣A. South takes another spade finesse and if West follows, South draws the last trump and takes the balance regardless of who has the ♣J.

If West shows out on the second round of trump, two dummy entries will be needed. West can be finessed for the ♣J.

The second alternative for handling a 4-1 spade break requires East to have 3 or more hearts. South plays a low club to the dummy on the first round. When the second round of trump reveals the 4-1 break, South should next hope to cash 3 rounds of hearts.

South crosses again in clubs and leads North's good heart. If East pitches, South discards his diamond and remains in dummy to finesse in spades.

If East ruffs dummy's last heart, South overruffs and draws the last trump. North has a trump remaining for South's diamond loser.

Assuming East has 4 spades, he has only 6 known cards (4 spades and 2 diamonds). West has 7 known cards (1 spade and 6 diamonds). Therefore, East is a favourite to hold at least 3 hearts and he is also more likely to hold the ♣J. Consequently, South should choose the second alternative over the entry club finesse.
